items.title: Frank Chace Interview, 1961-11-18
items.q: I know Gordon's playing, and I admire him enormously, although I resent and envy him.

ctx.x: So Marsala, as well, tried to emulate that.

So it might easily have extended through a couple of generations. Now, Marsala, in turn, has a new pupil, a fellow lately in town by the name of Bob Gordon, who is considerably respected. We'll watch and see if Noon, by any chance, gets all the way through to Gordon. That might happen.

Well, I certainly hope so. And I think there's a good chance of it, John. I know Gordon's playing, and I admire him enormously, although I resent and envy him. He's going to take my jobs away from me. He's 19. I think he's just turned 20. I don't know. He's going on the road with Muggsy Spanier next Monday, by the way. He adulates Marsala, and I think he has a great deal of the same lightness and deftness about his playing that Marsala showed. There's a sprightliness about Marsala's playing, never mind the tempo…
